en.19:27: Then Peter answered, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?”
en.19:28: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
en.19:29: Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit eternal life.
en.19:30: But many will be last who are first, and first who are last.
en.20:1: “For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who was the master of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.
en.20:2: When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
en.20:3: He went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
en.20:4: He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.’ So they went their way.
en.20:5: Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did likewise.
en.20:6: About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing idle. He said to them, ‘Why do you stand here all day idle?’
en.20:7: “They said to him, ‘Because no one has hired us.’ “He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and you will receive whatever is right.’
en.20:8: “When evening had come, the lord of the vineyard said to his manager, ‘Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last to the first.’
en.20:9: “When those who were hired at about the eleventh hour came, they each received a denarius.
en.20:10: When the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise each received a denarius.
en.20:11: When they received it, they murmured against the master of the household,
en.20:12: saying, ‘These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’
en.20:13: “But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?
en.20:14: Take that which is yours, and go your way. It is my desire to give to this last just as much as to you.
en.20:15: Isn’t it lawful for me to do what I want to with what I own? Or is your eye evil, because I am good?’
en.20:16: So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”
en.20:17: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, and on the way he said to them,
en.20:18: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,
en.20:19: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, to scourge, and to crucify; and the third day he will be raised up.”
en.20:20: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, kneeling and asking a certain thing of him.
en.20:21: He said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Command that these, my two sons, may sit, one on your right hand and one on your left hand, in your Kingdom.”
en.20:22: But Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?” They said to him, “We are able.”
en.20:23: He said to them, “You will indeed drink my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with; but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give, but it is for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”
en.20:24: When the ten heard it, they were indignant with the two brothers.
en.20:25: But Jesus summoned them, and said, “You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
en.20:26: It shall not be so among you; but whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant.
en.20:27: Whoever desires to be first among you shall be your bondservant,
en.20:28: even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
en.20:29: As they went out from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.
en.20:30: Behold, two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”
en.20:31: The multitude rebuked them, telling them that they should be quiet, but they cried out even more, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”
en.20:32: Jesus stood still and called them, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
en.20:33: They told him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”
en.20:34: Jesus, being moved with compassion, touched their eyes; and immediately their eyes received their sight, and they followed him.
en.21:1: When they came near to Jerusalem and came to Bethsphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
en.21:2: saying to them, “Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me.
en.21:3: If anyone says anything to you, you shall say, ‘The Lord needs them,’ and immediately he will send them.”
en.21:4: All this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,
en.21:5: “Tell the daughter of Zion, behold, your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.”
en.21:6: The disciples went and did just as Jesus commanded them,
en.21:7: and brought the donkey and the colt and laid their clothes on them; and he sat on them.
en.21:8: A very great multitude spread their clothes on the road. Others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
en.21:9: The multitudes who went in front of him, and those who followed, kept shouting, “Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
en.21:10: When he had come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred up, saying, “Who is this?”
en.21:11: The multitudes said, “This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”
en.21:12: Jesus entered into the temple of God and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.
en.21:13: He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of robbers!”
en.21:14: The lame and the blind came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
en.21:15: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children who were crying in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the son of David!” they were indignant,
en.21:16: and said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them, “Yes. Did you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of children and nursing babies, you have perfected praise’?”
en.21:17: He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, and camped there.
en.21:18: Now in the morning, as he returned to the city, he was hungry.
en.21:19: Seeing a fig tree by the road, he came to it and found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it, “Let there be no fruit from you forever!” Immediately the fig tree withered away.
en.21:20: When the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree immediately wither away?”
en.21:21: Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, if you have faith and don’t doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you told this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ it would be done.
en.21:22: All things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.”
en.21:23: When he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, “By what authority do you do these things? Who gave you this authority?”
en.21:24: Jesus answered them, “I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
en.21:25: The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?” They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
en.21:26: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.”
en.21:27: They answered Jesus, and said, “We don’t know.” He also said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
en.21:28: But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’
en.21:29: He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went.
en.21:30: He came to the second, and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’m going, sir,’ but he didn’t go.
en.21:31: Which of the two did the will of his father?” They said to him, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering into God’s Kingdom before you.
en.21:32: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. When you saw it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.
en.21:33: “Hear another parable. There was a man who was a master of a household who planted a vineyard, set a hedge about it, dug a wine press in it, built a tower, leased it out to farmers, and went into another country.
en.21:34: When the season for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the farmers to receive his fruit.
en.21:35: The farmers took his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
en.21:36: Again, he sent other servants more than the first; and they treated them the same way.
en.21:37: But afterward he sent to them his son, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
en.21:38: But the farmers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him and seize his inheritance.’
en.21:39: So they took him and threw him out of the vineyard, then killed him.
en.21:40: When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
en.21:41: They told him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will lease out the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruit in its season.”
en.21:42: Jesus said to them, “Did you never read in the Scriptures, ‘The stone which the builders rejected was made the head of the corner. This was from the Lord. It is marvelous in our eyes’?
en.21:43: “Therefore I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you and will be given to a nation producing its fruit.
en.21:44: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but on whomever it will fall, it will scatter him as dust.”
en.21:45: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spoke about them.
en.21:46: When they sought to seize him, they feared the multitudes, because they considered him to be a prophet.
en.22:1: Jesus answered and spoke to them again in parables, saying,
en.22:2: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king, who made a wedding feast for his son,
en.22:3: and sent out his servants to call those who were invited to the wedding feast, but they would not come.
en.22:4: Again he sent out other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who are invited, “Behold, I have prepared my dinner. My cattle and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the wedding feast!”’
en.22:5: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;
en.22:6: and the rest grabbed his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them.
en.22:7: When the king heard that, he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
en.22:8: “Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding is ready, but those who were invited weren’t worthy.
en.22:9: Go therefore to the intersections of the highways, and as many as you may find, invite to the wedding feast.’
en.22:10: Those servants went out into the highways and gathered together as many as they found, both bad and good. The wedding was filled with guests.
en.22:11: “But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who didn’t have on wedding clothing,
en.22:12: and he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here not wearing wedding clothing?’ He was speechless.
en.22:13: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and throw him into the outer darkness. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.’
en.22:14: For many are called, but few chosen.”
en.22:15: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might entrap him in his talk.
en.22:16: They sent their disciples to him, along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and teach the way of God in truth, no matter whom you teach; for you aren’t partial to anyone.
en.22:17: Tell us therefore, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
en.22:18: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, “Why do you test me, you hypocrites?
en.22:19: Show me the tax money.” They brought to him a denarius.
en.22:20: He asked them, “Whose is this image and inscription?”
en.22:21: They said to him, “Caesar’s.” Then he said to them, “Give therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
en.22:22: When they heard it, they marveled, and left him and went away.
en.22:23: On that day Sadducees (those who say that there is no resurrection) came to him. They asked him,
en.22:24: saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
en.22:25: Now there were with us seven brothers. The first married and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.
en.22:26: In the same way, the second also, and the third, to the seventh.
en.22:27: After them all, the woman died.
en.22:28: In the resurrection therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.”
en.22:29: But Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.
en.22:30: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.
en.22:31: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
en.22:32: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
en.22:33: When the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.
en.22:34: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, gathered themselves together.
en.22:35: One of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, testing him.
en.22:36: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the law?”
en.22:37: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
en.22:38: This is the first and great commandment.
en.22:39: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
en.22:40: The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”
en.22:41: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,
en.22:42: saying, “What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “Of David.”
en.22:43: He said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
en.22:44: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, sit on my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet’?
en.22:45: “If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”
en.22:46: No one was able to answer him a word, neither did any man dare ask him any more questions from that day forward.
en.23:1: Then Jesus spoke to the multitudes and to his disciples,
en.23:2: saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.
en.23:3: All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do, but don’t do their works; for they say, and don’t do.
en.23:4: For they bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not lift a finger to help them.
en.23:5: But they do all their works to be seen by men. They make their phylacteries broad and enlarge the fringes of their garments,
en.23:6: and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,
en.23:7: the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’ by men.
en.23:8: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi’, for one is your teacher, the Christ, and all of you are brothers.
en.23:9: Call no man on the earth your father, for one is your Father, he who is in heaven.
en.23:10: Neither be called masters, for one is your master, the Christ.
en.23:11: But he who is greatest among you will be your servant.
en.23:12: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
en.23:13: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.
en.23:14: “But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you shut up the Kingdom of Heaven against men; for you don’t enter in yourselves, neither do you allow those who are entering in to enter.
en.23:15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.
en.23:16: “Woe to you, you blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, he is obligated.’
en.23:17: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that sanctifies the gold?
en.23:18: And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it, he is obligated.’
en.23:19: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
en.23:20: He therefore who swears by the altar, swears by it and by everything on it.
en.23:21: He who swears by the temple, swears by it and by him who has been living in it.
en.23:22: He who swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God and by him who sits on it.
en.23:23: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
en.23:24: You blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel!
en.23:25: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and unrighteousness.
en.23:26: You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the platter, that its outside may become clean also.
en.23:27: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones and of all uncleanness.
en.23:28: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
en.23:29: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the tombs of the righteous,
en.23:30: and say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we wouldn’t have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.’
en.23:31: Therefore you testify to yourselves that you are children of those who killed the prophets.
en.23:32: Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers.
en.23:33: You serpents, you offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?
en.23:34: Therefore, behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify; and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
en.23:35: that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.
en.23:36: Most certainly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
en.23:37: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!
en.23:38: Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
en.23:39: For I tell you, you will not see me from now on, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
en.24:1: Jesus went out from the temple, and was going on his way. His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
en.24:2: But he answered them, “You see all of these things, don’t you? Most certainly I tell you, there will not be left here one stone on another, that will not be thrown down.”
en.24:3: As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign of your coming, and of the end of the age?”
en.24:4: Jesus answered them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
en.24:5: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
en.24:6: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you aren’t troubled, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.
en.24:7: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there will be famines, plagues, and earthquakes in various places.
en.24:8: But all these things are the beginning of birth pains.
en.24:9: “Then they will deliver you up to oppression and will kill you. You will be hated by all of the nations for my name’s sake.
en.24:10: Then many will stumble, and will deliver up one another, and will hate one another.
en.24:11: Many false prophets will arise and will lead many astray.
en.24:12: Because iniquity will be multiplied, the love of many will grow cold.
en.24:13: But he who endures to the end will be saved.
en.24:14: This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
en.24:15: “When, therefore, you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),
en.24:16: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
en.24:17: Let him who is on the housetop not go down to take out the things that are in his house.
en.24:18: Let him who is in the field not return back to get his clothes.
en.24:19: But woe to those who are with child and to nursing mothers in those days!
en.24:20: Pray that your flight will not be in the winter nor on a Sabbath,
en.24:21: for then there will be great suffering, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, no, nor ever will be.
en.24:22: Unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be shortened.
en.24:23: “Then if any man tells you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘There!’ don’t believe it.
en.24:24: For false christs and false prophets will arise, and they will show great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
en.24:26: “If therefore they tell you, ‘Behold, he is in the wilderness,’ don’t go out; or ‘Behold, he is in the inner rooms,’ don’t believe it.
en.24:27: For as the lightning flashes from the east, and is seen even to the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
en.24:28: For wherever the carcass is, that is where the vultures gather together.
en.24:29: “But immediately after the suffering of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken;
en.24:30: and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
en.24:31: He will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.
en.24:32: “Now from the fig tree learn this parable: When its branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near.
en.24:33: Even so you also, when you see all these things, know that he is near, even at the doors.
en.24:34: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things are accomplished.
en.24:35: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
en.24:36: “But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
en.24:37: As the days of Noah were, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
en.24:38: For as in those days which were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship,
en.24:39: and they didn’t know until the flood came and took them all away, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
en.24:40: Then two men will be in the field: one will be taken and one will be left.
en.24:41: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and one will be left.
en.24:42: Watch therefore, for you don’t know in what hour your Lord comes.
en.24:43: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have watched, and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
en.24:44: Therefore also be ready, for in an hour that you don’t expect, the Son of Man will come.
en.24:45: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has set over his household, to give them their food in due season?
en.24:46: Blessed is that servant whom his lord finds doing so when he comes.
en.24:47: Most certainly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.
en.24:48: But if that evil servant should say in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’
en.24:49: and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eat and drink with the drunkards,
en.24:50: the lord of that servant will come in a day when he doesn’t expect it and in an hour when he doesn’t know it,
en.24:51: and will cut him in pieces and appoint his portion with the hypocrites. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.
en.25:1: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
en.25:2: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
en.25:3: Those who were foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them,
en.25:4: but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
en.25:5: Now while the bridegroom delayed, they all slumbered and slept.
en.25:6: But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Behold! The bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!’
en.25:7: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.
en.25:8: The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’
en.25:9: But the wise answered, saying, ‘What if there isn’t enough for us and you? You go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.’
en.25:10: While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
en.25:11: Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’
en.25:12: But he answered, ‘Most certainly I tell you, I don’t know you.’
en.25:13: Watch therefore, for you don’t know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.
en.25:14: “For it is like a man going into another country, who called his own servants and entrusted his goods to them.
en.25:15: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his own ability. Then he went on his journey.
en.25:16: Immediately he who received the five talents went and traded with them, and made another five talents.
en.25:17: In the same way, he also who got the two gained another two.
en.25:18: But he who received the one talent went away and dug in the earth and hid his lord’s money.
en.25:19: “Now after a long time the lord of those servants came, and settled accounts with them.
en.25:20: He who received the five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents. Behold, I have gained another five talents in addition to them.’
en.25:21: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
en.25:22: “He also who got the two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. Behold, I have gained another two talents in addition to them.’
en.25:23: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things. I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
en.25:24: “He also who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Lord, I knew you that you are a hard man, reaping where you didn’t sow, and gathering where you didn’t scatter.
en.25:25: I was afraid, and went away and hid your talent in the earth. Behold, you have what is yours.’
en.25:26: “But his lord answered him, ‘You wicked and slothful servant. You knew that I reap where I didn’t sow, and gather where I didn’t scatter.
en.25:27: You ought therefore to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I should have received back my own with interest.
en.25:28: Take away therefore the talent from him and give it to him who has the ten talents.
en.25:29: For to everyone who has will be given, and he will have abundance, but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away.
en.25:30: Throw out the unprofitable servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
en.25:31: “But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
en.25:32: Before him all the nations will be gathered, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
en.25:33: He will set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.
en.25:34: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
en.25:35: for I was hungry and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty and you gave me drink. I was a stranger and you took me in.
en.25:36: I was naked and you clothed me. I was sick and you visited me. I was in prison and you came to me.’
en.25:37: “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?
en.25:38: When did we see you as a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
en.25:39: When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’
en.25:40: “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’
en.25:41: Then he will say also to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels;
en.25:42: for I was hungry, and you didn’t give me food to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink;
en.25:43: I was a stranger, and you didn’t take me in; naked, and you didn’t clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’
en.25:44: “Then they will also answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and didn’t help you?’
en.25:45: “Then he will answer them, saying, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you didn’t do it to one of the least of these, you didn’t do it to me.’
en.25:46: These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
en.26:1: When Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
en.26:2: “You know that after two days the Passover is coming, and the Son of Man will be delivered up to be crucified.”
en.26:3: Then the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people were gathered together in the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
en.26:4: They took counsel together that they might take Jesus by deceit and kill him.
en.26:5: But they said, “Not during the feast, lest a riot occur among the people.”
en.26:6: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
en.26:7: a woman came to him having an alabaster jar of very expensive ointment, and she poured it on his head as he sat at the table.
en.26:8: But when his disciples saw this, they were indignant, saying, “Why this waste?
en.26:9: For this ointment might have been sold for much and given to the poor.”
en.26:10: However, knowing this, Jesus said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? She has done a good work for me.
en.26:11: For you always have the poor with you, but you don’t always have me.
en.26:12: For in pouring this ointment on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
en.26:13: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of as a memorial of her.”
en.26:14: Then one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
en.26:15: and said, “What are you willing to give me if I deliver him to you?” So they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.
en.26:16: From that time he sought opportunity to betray him.
en.26:17: Now on the first day of unleavened bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying to him, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”
en.26:18: He said, “Go into the city to a certain person, and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is at hand. I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”
en.26:19: The disciples did as Jesus commanded them, and they prepared the Passover.
en.26:20: Now when evening had come, he was reclining at the table with the twelve disciples.
en.26:21: As they were eating, he said, “Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me.”
en.26:22: They were exceedingly sorrowful, and each began to ask him, “It isn’t me, is it, Lord?”
en.26:23: He answered, “He who dipped his hand with me in the dish will betray me.
en.26:24: The Son of Man goes even as it is written of him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
en.26:25: Judas, who betrayed him, answered, “It isn’t me, is it, Rabbi?” He said to him, “You said it.”
en.26:26: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks for it, and broke it. He gave to the disciples and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”
en.26:27: He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave to them, saying, “All of you drink it,
en.26:28: for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins.
en.26:29: But I tell you that I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”
en.26:30: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
en.26:31: Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
en.26:32: But after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
en.26:33: But Peter answered him, “Even if all will be made to stumble because of you, I will never be made to stumble.”
en.26:34: Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you that tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
en.26:35: Peter said to him, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” All of the disciples also said likewise.
en.26:36: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to his disciples, “Sit here, while I go there and pray.”
en.26:37: He took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and severely troubled.
en.26:38: Then Jesus said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch with me.”
en.26:39: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
en.26:40: He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “What, couldn’t you watch with me for one hour?
en.26:41: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
en.26:42: Again, a second time he went away and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cup can’t pass away from me unless I drink it, your desire be done.”
en.26:43: He came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
en.26:44: He left them again, went away, and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
en.26:45: Then he came to his disciples and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
en.26:46: Arise, let’s be going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”
en.26:47: While he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
en.26:48: Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “Whoever I kiss, he is the one. Seize him.”
en.26:49: Immediately he came to Jesus, and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him.
en.26:50: Jesus said to him, “Friend, why are you here?” Then they came and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.
en.26:51: Behold, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand and drew his sword, and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
en.26:52: Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.
en.26:53: Or do you think that I couldn’t ask my Father, and he would even now send me more than twelve legions of angels?
en.26:54: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that it must be so?”
en.26:55: In that hour Jesus said to the multitudes, “Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me? I sat daily in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me.
en.26:56: But all this has happened that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him and fled.
en.26:57: Those who had taken Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered together.
en.26:58: But Peter followed him from a distance to the court of the high priest, and entered in and sat with the officers, to see the end.
en.26:59: Now the chief priests, the elders, and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus, that they might put him to death,
en.26:60: and they found none. Even though many false witnesses came forward, they found none. But at last two false witnesses came forward
en.26:61: and said, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.’”
en.26:62: The high priest stood up and said to him, “Have you no answer? What is this that these testify against you?”
en.26:63: But Jesus stayed silent. The high priest answered him, “I adjure you by the living God that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
en.26:64: Jesus said to him, “You have said so. Nevertheless, I tell you, after this you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming on the clouds of the sky.”
en.26:65: Then the high priest tore his clothing, saying, “He has spoken blasphemy! Why do we need any more witnesses? Behold, now you have heard his blasphemy.
en.26:66: What do you think?” They answered, “He is worthy of death!”
en.26:67: Then they spat in his face and beat him with their fists, and some slapped him,
en.26:68: saying, “Prophesy to us, you Christ! Who hit you?”
en.26:69: Now Peter was sitting outside in the court, and a maid came to him, saying, “You were also with Jesus, the Galilean!”
en.26:70: But he denied it before them all, saying, “I don’t know what you are talking about.”
en.26:71: When he had gone out onto the porch, someone else saw him and said to those who were there, “This man also was with Jesus of Nazareth.”
en.26:72: Again he denied it with an oath, “I don’t know the man.”
en.26:73: After a little while those who stood by came and said to Peter, “Surely you are also one of them, for your speech makes you known.”
en.26:74: Then he began to curse and to swear, “I don’t know the man!” Immediately the rooster crowed.
en.26:75: Peter remembered the word which Jesus had said to him, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” Then he went out and wept bitterly.
en.27:1: Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.
en.27:2: They bound him, led him away, and delivered him up to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
en.27:3: Then Judas, who betrayed him, when he saw that Jesus was condemned, felt remorse, and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
en.27:4: saying, “I have sinned in that I betrayed innocent blood.” But they said, “What is that to us? You see to it.”
en.27:5: He threw down the pieces of silver in the sanctuary and departed. Then he went away and hanged himself.
en.27:6: The chief priests took the pieces of silver and said, “It’s not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is the price of blood.”
en.27:7: They took counsel, and bought the potter’s field with them to bury strangers in.
en.27:8: Therefore that field has been called “The Field of Blood” to this day.
en.27:9: Then that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying, “They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him upon whom a price had been set, whom some of the children of Israel priced,
en.27:10: and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord commanded me.”
en.27:11: Now Jesus stood before the governor; and the governor asked him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “So you say.”
en.27:12: When he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.
en.27:13: Then Pilate said to him, “Don’t you hear how many things they testify against you?”
en.27:14: He gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
en.27:15: Now at the feast the governor was accustomed to release to the multitude one prisoner whom they desired.
en.27:16: They had then a notable prisoner called Barabbas.
en.27:17: When therefore they were gathered together, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
en.27:18: For he knew that because of envy they had delivered him up.
en.27:19: While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered many things today in a dream because of him.”
en.27:20: Now the chief priests and the elders persuaded the multitudes to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus.
en.27:21: But the governor answered them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas!”
en.27:22: Pilate said to them, “What then shall I do to Jesus who is called Christ?” They all said to him, “Let him be crucified!”
en.27:23: But the governor said, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, saying, “Let him be crucified!”
en.27:24: So when Pilate saw that nothing was being gained, but rather that a disturbance was starting, he took water and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous person. You see to it.”
en.27:25: All the people answered, “May his blood be on us and on our children!”
en.27:26: Then he released Barabbas to them, but Jesus he flogged and delivered to be crucified.
en.27:27: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
en.27:28: They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him.
en.27:29: They braided a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and they kneeled down before him and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
en.27:30: They spat on him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.
en.27:31: When they had mocked him, they took the robe off him, and put his clothes on him, and led him away to crucify him.
en.27:32: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they compelled him to go with them, that he might carry his cross.
en.27:33: When they came to a place called “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of a skull,”
en.27:34: they gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.
en.27:35: When they had crucified him, they divided his clothing among them, casting lots,
en.27:36: and they sat and watched him there.
en.27:37: They set up over his head the accusation against him written, “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
en.27:38: Then there were two robbers crucified with him, one on his right hand and one on the left.
en.27:39: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads
en.27:40: and saying, “You who destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
en.27:41: Likewise the chief priests also mocking with the scribes, the Pharisees, and the elders, said,
en.27:42: “He saved others, but he can’t save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.
en.27:43: He trusts in God. Let God deliver him now, if he wants him; for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
en.27:44: The robbers also who were crucified with him cast on him the same reproach.
en.27:45: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
en.27:46: About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
en.27:47: Some of them who stood there, when they heard it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
en.27:48: Immediately one of them ran and took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
en.27:49: The rest said, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to save him.”
en.27:50: Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.
en.27:51: Behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
en.27:52: The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised;
en.27:53: and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they entered into the holy city and appeared to many.
en.27:54: Now the centurion and those who were with him watching Jesus, when they saw the earthquake and the things that were done, were terrified, saying, “Truly this was the Son of God!”
en.27:55: Many women were there watching from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
en.27:56: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
en.27:57: When evening had come, a rich man from Arimathaea named Joseph, who himself was also Jesus’ disciple, came.
en.27:58: This man went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate commanded the body to be given up.
en.27:59: Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth
en.27:60: and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock. Then he rolled a large stone against the door of the tomb, and departed.
en.27:61: Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
en.27:62: Now on the next day, which was the day after the Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together to Pilate,
en.27:63: saying, “Sir, we remember what that deceiver said while he was still alive: ‘After three days I will rise again.’
en.27:64: Command therefore that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come at night and steal him away, and tell the people, ‘He is risen from the dead;’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
en.27:65: Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go, make it as secure as you can.”
en.27:66: So they went with the guard and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone.
en.28:1: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
en.28:2: Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky and came and rolled away the stone from the door and sat on it.
en.28:3: His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
en.28:4: For fear of him, the guards shook, and became like dead men.
en.28:5: The angel answered the women, “Don’t be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified.
en.28:6: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.
en.28:7: Go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Behold, I have told you.”
en.28:8: They departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring his disciples word.
en.28:9: As they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Rejoice!” They came and took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
en.28:10: Then Jesus said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
en.28:11: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
en.28:12: When they were assembled with the elders and had taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
en.28:13: saying, “Say that his disciples came by night and stole him away while we slept.
en.28:14: If this comes to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you free of worry.”
en.28:15: So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
en.28:16: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
en.28:17: When they saw him, they bowed down to him; but some doubted.
en.28:18: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
en.28:19: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
en.28:20: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

pl.1:1: Księgi rodzaju Jezusa Chrystusa, syna Dawidowego, syna Abrahamowego.
pl.1:2: Abraham zrodził Izaaka. A Izaak zrodził Jakóba. A Jakób zrodził Judę i bracią jego.
pl.1:3: A Judas zrodził Pharesa i Zarę z Thamar. A Phares zrodził Esrona. A Esron zrodził Aram.
pl.1:4: A Aram zrodził Aminadaba. Aminadab zrodził Naasson. A Naasson zrodził Salmona.
pl.1:5: A Salmon zrodził Booza z Rahab. A Booz zrodził Obeda z Ruth. A Obed zrodził Jesse. A Jesse zrodził Dawida króla.
pl.1:6: A Dawid król zrodził Salomona z téj, która była Uryaszowa.
pl.1:7: A Salomon zrodził Roboama. A Roboam zrodził Abia. A Abia zrodził Asę.
pl.1:8: A Asa zrodził Jozaphata. A Jozaphat zrodził Jorama. A Joram zrodził Ozyasza.
pl.1:9: A Ozyasz zrodził Joathama. A Joatham zrodził Achaza. A Achaz zrodził Ezechiasza.
pl.1:10: A Ezechiasz zrodził Manassesa. A Manasses zrodził Amona. A Amon zrodził Jozyasza.
pl.1:11: A Jozyasz zrodził Jechoniasza i bracią jego, w przeprowadzeniu Babilońskiem.
pl.1:12: A po przeprowadzeniu Babilońskiem, Jechoniasz zrodził Salathiela. A Salathiel zrodził Zorobabela.
pl.1:13: A Zorobabel zrodził Abiuda. A Abiud zrodził Eliacyma. A Eliacym zrodził Azora.
pl.1:14: A Azor zrodził Sadoka. A Sadok zrodził Achima. A Achim zrodził Eliuda.
pl.1:15: A Eliud zrodził Eleazara. A Eleazar zrodził Matthana. A Matthan zrodził Jakóba.
pl.1:16: A Jakób zrodził Józepha, męża Maryi, z któréj się narodził Jezus, którego zowią Chrystusem.
pl.1:17: A tak wszystkiego pokolenia, od Abrahama aż do Dawida, pokolenia czternaście, a od Dawida aż do przeprowadzenia Babilońskiego, pokolenia czternaście, a od przeprowadzenia Babilońskiego aż do Chrystusa, pokolenia czternaście.
pl.1:18: A narodzenie Chrystusowe tak było: Gdy była poślubiona matka jego Marya Józephowi, pierwéj niźli się zeszli, naleziona jest w żywocie mająca z Ducha Świętego.
pl.1:19: A Józeph, mąż jéj, będąc sprawiedliwym i nie chcąc jéj osławiać, chciał ją potajemnie opuścić.
pl.1:20: A gdy to on myślił, oto Aniół Pański ukazał mu się we śnie, mówiąc: Józephie, synu Dawidów! nie bój się przyjąć Maryi, małżonki twéj; albowiem co się w niéj urodziło, jest z Ducha Świętego.
pl.1:21: A porodzi syna, i nazowiesz imię jego Jezus; albowiem on zbawi lud swój od grzechów ich.
pl.1:22: A to się wszystko stało, aby się wypełniło, co jest powiedziano od Pana przez proroka mówiącego:
pl.1:23: Oto panna w żywocie mieć będzie i porodzi syna, i nazowią imię jego Emanuel, co się wykłada: Bóg z nami.
pl.1:24: A Józeph wstawszy ze snu, uczynił, jako mu rozkazał Aniół Pański, i przyjął żonę swoję.
pl.1:25: I nie uznał jéj, aż porodziła syna swego pierworodnego, i nazwał imię jego Jezus. Gdy się tedy narodził Jezus w Bethlehem Juda, we dni Heroda króla: oto Mędrcy ze wschodu słońca przybyli do Jerozolimy,
pl.2:2: Mówiąc: Gdzie jest, który się narodził król Żydowski? Albowiem widzieliśmy gwiazdę jego na wschód słońca, i przyjechaliśmy pokłonić się jemu.
pl.2:3: A usłyszawszy król Herod, zatrwożył się, i wszystka Jerozolima z nim.
pl.2:4: I zebrawszy wszystkie przedniejsze kapłany i Doktory ludu, dowiadował się od nich, gdzie się miał Chrystus narodzić.
pl.2:5: A oni mu rzekli: W Bethlehem Judzkiem; bo tak jest napisano przez proroka:
pl.2:6: I ty Bethlehem, ziemio Judzka! z żadnéj miary nie jesteś najpodlejsze między książęty Judzkiemi; albowiem z ciebie wynidzie wódz, któryby rządził lud mój Izraelski.
pl.2:7: Tedy Herod wezwawszy potajemnie Mędrców, pilnie się wywiadował od nich czasu gwiazdy, która się im ukazała.
pl.2:8: I posławszy je do Bethlehem, rzekł: Idźcie a wywiadujcie się pilno o dzieciątku; a gdy najdziecie, oznajmijcie mi, abym i ja przyjechawszy pokłonił się jemu.
pl.2:9: Którzy wysłuchawszy króla, odjechali. A oto gwiazda, którą byli widzieli na wschód słońca, szła przed nimi, aż przyszedłszy stanęła nad miejscem, gdzie było dziecię.
pl.2:10: A ujrzawszy gwiazdę, uradowali się radością bardzo wielką.
pl.2:11: I wszedłszy w dom, naleźli dziecię z Maryą, matką jego, i upadłszy pokłonili się jemu, a otworzywszy skarby swe, ofiarowali mu dary, złoto, kadzidło i mirrhę.
pl.2:12: A wziąwszy odpowiedź we śnie, aby się nie wracali do Heroda, inszą drogą wrócili się do krainy swojéj.
pl.2:13: Którzy gdy odjechali, oto Aniół Pański ukazał się we śnie Józephowi, mówiąc: Wstań a weźmij dziecię i matkę jego, a uciecz do Egiptu i bądź tam, aż ci powiem; albowiem będzie, że Herod szukać będzie dziecięcia, aby je zatracił.
pl.2:14: Który wstawszy, wziął dziecię i matkę jego w nocy i uszedł do Egiptu.
pl.2:15: I był tam aż do śmierci Herodowéj: aby się spełniło, co powiedziano jest od Pana przez proroka mówiącego: Z Egiptu wezwałem Syna mojego.
pl.2:16: Tedy Herod widząc, że był omylonym od Mędrców, rozgniewał się bardzo i posławszy pobił wszystkie dzieci, które były w Bethlehem i po wszystkich granicach jego, ode dwu lat i niżéj, według czasu, którego się był wypytał od Mędrców.
pl.2:17: Tedy się wypełniło, co jest rzeczone przez Jeremiasza proroka, mówiącego:
pl.2:18: Głos jest słyszan w Ramie, płacz i krzyk wielki: Rachel płacząca synów swoich i nie chciała się dać pocieszyć, iż ich niemasz.
pl.2:19: A gdy Herod umarł, oto Aniół Pański ukazał się we śnie Józephowi w Egipcie, mówiąc:
pl.2:20: Wstań a weźmij dziecię i matkę jego, a idź do ziemie Izraelskiéj; albowiem pomarli, którzy dusze dziecięcéj szukali.
pl.2:21: Który wstawszy, wziął dziecię i matkę jego i przyszedł do ziemie Izraelskiéj.
pl.2:22: A usłyszawszy, iż Archelaus królował w Żydowskiéj ziemi miasto Heroda, ojca swego, bał się tam iść; a napomniony we śnie, ustąpił w strony Galilejskie.
pl.2:23: A przyszedłszy mieszkał w mieście, które zowią Nazareth, aby się wypełniło, co rzeczono jest przez proroki: Iż Nazarejskim będzie nazwany.
pl.3:1: A we dni one przyszedł Jan Chrzciciel, każąc na puszczy Żydowskiéj ziemie.
pl.3:2: I mówiąc: Czyńcie pokutę; albowiem przybliżyło się królestwo niebieskie.
pl.3:3: Bowiem ten jest, który opowiedziany jest przez Izajasza proroka, mówiącego: Głos wołającego na puszczy: Gotujcie drogę Pańską, proste czyńcie ścieżki jego.
pl.3:4: A ten Jan miał odzienie z sierci wielbłądowéj i pas skórzany około biódr swoich, a pokarm jego był szarańcze i miód leśny.
pl.3:5: Tedy wychodziło do niego Jeruzalem i wszystka Żydowska ziemia i wszystek kraj około Jordanu.
pl.3:6: I byli chrzczeni w Jordanie od niego, spowiadając się grzechów swoich.
pl.3:7: A gdy widział wielu z Pharyzeuszów i Sadduceuszów przychodzących do chrztu swego, mówił im: Rodzaju jaszczórczy! któż wam pokazał, abyście uciekali od przyszłego gniewu?
pl.3:9: A nie chciejcie mówić sami w sobie: Ojca mamy Abrahama. Albowiem wam powiadam, iż mocen jest Bóg, z kamienia tego wzbudzić syny Abrahamowi.
pl.3:10: Bo już siekiera do korzenia drzew jest przyłożona. Przeto wszelkie drzewo, które nie daje owocu dobrego, będzie wycięte i w ogień wrzucone.
pl.3:11: Jać was chrzczę wodą ku pokucie: ale który przyjdzie po mnie, mocniejszy jest niż ja, któregom trzewików nie jest godzien nosić; tenci was ochrzci Duchem Ś. i ogniem.
pl.3:12: Którego łopata w ręku jego, a wyczyści bojewisko swoje i zgromadzi pszenicę swą do gumna, a plewy spali ogniem nieugaszonym.
pl.3:13: Tedy Jezus przyszedł od Galilei do Jordanu do Jana, aby był ochrzczon od niego.
pl.3:14: A Jan mu nie dopuszczał, mówiąc: Ja mam być ochrzczon od ciebie, a ty idziesz do mnie?
pl.3:15: A Jezus odpowiadając rzekł mu: Zaniechaj teraz; albowiem tak się nam godzi wypełnić wszelką sprawiedliwość. I tak go dopuścił.
pl.3:16: A gdy był Jezus ochrzczony, wnet wystąpił z wody. A oto się otworzyły jemu niebiosa, i widział Ducha Bożego zstępującego jako gołębicę i przychodzącego nań.
pl.3:17: I oto głos z niebios mówiący: Ten jest Syn mój miły, w którymem upodobał sobie.
pl.4:1: Tedy Jezus był zawiedzion na puszczą od Ducha, aby był kuszon od djabła.
pl.4:2: A gdy pościł czterdzieści dni i czterdzieści nocy, potem łaknął.
pl.4:3: I przystąpiwszy kusiciel, rzekł mu: Jeźliś jest syn Boży, rzecz, aby to kamienie stało się chlebem.
pl.4:4: Który odpowiadając, rzekł: Napisano jest: Nie samym chlebem żywie człowiek; ale wszelkiem słowem, które pochodzi z ust Bożych.
pl.4:5: Tedy go wziął djabeł do miasta świętego i postawił go na ganku kościelnym.
pl.4:6: I rzekł mu: Jeźliś jest Syn Boży, spuść się nadół; albowiem napisano jest: Iż Aniołom swoim rozkazał o tobie, i będą cię na ręku nosić, abyś snadź nie obraził o kamień nogi swojéj.
pl.4:7: Rzekł mu Jezus: Zasię napisano jest: Nie będziesz kusił Pana, Boga twego.
pl.4:8: Wziął go zaś djabeł na górę wysoką bardzo i ukazał mu wszystkie królestwa świata i chwałę ich,
pl.4:9: I rzekł mu: To wszystko dam tobie, jeźli upadłszy uczynisz mi pokłon.
pl.4:10: Tedy mu rzekł Jezus: Pójdź precz, szatanie! albowiem napisano jest: Panu Bogu twemu kłaniać się będziesz, a jemu samemu służyć będziesz.
pl.4:11: Tedy opuścił go djabeł, a oto Aniołowie przystąpili i służyli jemu.
pl.4:12: A gdy usłyszał Jezus, iż Jan był wydan, uszedł do Galilei.
pl.4:13: I opuściwszy miasto Nazareth, przyszedł i mieszkał w Kapharnaum nad morzem, na granicach Zabulon i Nephthalim.
pl.4:14: Aby się wypełniło, co jest rzeczono przez Izajasza proroka:
pl.4:15: Ziemia Zabulon i ziemia Nephthalim, droga morska za Jordanem, Galilea poganów.
pl.4:16: Lud, który siedział w ciemności, ujrzał światłość wielką, i siedzącym w krainie cienia śmierci, weszła im światłość.
pl.4:17: Odtąd począł Jezus kazać i mówić: Pokutę czyńcie; albowiem przybliżyło się królestwo niebieskie.
pl.4:18: A gdy Jezus chodził nad morzem Galilejskiem, ujrzał dwu braciéj, Symona, którego zowią Piotrem, i Andrzeja, brata jego, zapuszczające sieci w morze; (albowiem byli rybitwi).
pl.4:19: I rzekł im: Pójdźcie za mną, a uczynię was, że się staniecie rybitwami ludzi.
pl.4:20: A oni natychmiast opuściwszy sieci, szli za nim.
pl.4:21: A postąpiwszy ztamtąd, ujrzał drugich dwu braciéj, Jakóba Zebedeuszowego, i Jana brata jego, w łodzi z Zebedeuszem, ojcem ich, oprawując sieci swoje, i wezwał ich.
pl.4:22: A oni natychmiast opuściwszy sieci i ojca, szli za nim.
pl.4:23: I obchodził Jezus wszystkę Galileą, nauczając w bóżnicach ich i przepowiadając Ewangelią królestwa a uzdrawiając wszelaką chorobę i wszelaką niemoc między ludem.
pl.4:24: I rozeszła się sława jego po wszystkiéj Syryi, i przynosili mu wszystkie źle się mające, rozmaitemi chorobami i dręczeniem zjęte, i którzy djabelstwa mieli, i lunatyki i powietrzem ruszone, i uzdrowił je.
pl.4:25: I szły za nim wielkie rzesze od Galilei i Dekapolu i Jeruzalem i z Żydowskiéj ziemie i z Zajordania.
pl.5:1: A widząc Jezus rzesze, wstąpił na górę, a gdy usiadł, przystąpili k niemu uczniowie jego.
pl.5:2: A otworzywszy usta swe, nauczał ich, mówiąc:
pl.5:3: Błogosławieni ubodzy duchem; albowiem ich jest królestwo niebieskie.
pl.5:4: Błogosławieni ciszy; albowiem oni posiędą ziemię.
pl.5:5: Błogosławieni, którzy płaczą; albowiem oni będą pocieszeni.
pl.5:6: Błogosławieni, którzy łakną i pragną sprawiedliwości; albowiem oni będą nasyceni.
pl.5:7: Błogosławieni miłosierni; albowiem oni miłosierdzia dostąpią.
pl.5:8: Błogosławieni czystego serca; albowiem oni Boga oglądają.
pl.5:9: Błogosławieni pokój czyniący; albowiem nazwani będą synami Bożymi.
pl.5:10: Błogosławieni, którzy cierpią prześladowanie dla sprawiedliwości; albowiem ich jest królestwo niebieskie.
pl.5:11: Błogosławieni jesteście, gdy wam złorzeczyć będą i prześladować was będą i mówić wszystko złe przeciwko wam kłamając, dla mnie.
pl.5:12: Radujcie się i weselcie się; albowiem zapłata wasza obfita jest w niebiesiech; boć tak prześladowali proroki, którzy przed wami byli.
pl.5:13: Wy jesteście sól ziemie. A jeźli sól zwietrzeje, czem solona będzie? Ninacz się więcéj nie zgodzi, jedno aby była precz wyrzucona i podeptana od ludzi.
pl.5:14: Wy jesteście światłość świata. Nie może się miasto zakryć na górze osadzone;
pl.5:15: Ani zapalają świece i kładą jéj pod korzec, ale na świeczniku, aby świeciła wszystkim, którzy są w domu.
pl.5:16: Tak niechaj świeci światłość wasza przed ludźmi, aby widzieli uczynki wasze dobre i chwalili Ojca waszego, który jest w niebiesiech.
pl.5:17: Nie mniemajcie, abym przyszedł rozwięzować zakon albo proroki. Nie przyszedłem rozwięzować, ale wypełnić.
pl.5:18: Zaprawdę bowiem powiadam wam: Aż przeminie niebo i ziemia, jedno jota, albo jedna kreska nie odmieni się w zakonie, aż się wszystko stanie.
pl.5:19: Ktoby tedy rozwiązał jedno z tych przykazań najmniejszych i takby ludzi nauczał, będzie zwann najmniejszym w królestwie niebieskiem, a ktoby czynił i nauczał, ten będzie zwań wielkim w królestwie niebieskiem.
pl.5:20: Albowiem powiadam wam, iż, jeźli nie będzie obfitowała sprawiedliwość wasza więcéj niż Doktorów zakonnych i Pharyzeuszów, nie wnidziecie do królestwa niebieskiego.
pl.5:21: Słyszeliście, iż rzeczono jest starym: Nie będziesz zabijał, a ktoby zabił, będzie winien sądu.
pl.5:22: A Ja wam powiadam, iż każdy, który się gniewa na brata swego, będzie winien sądu. A ktoby rzekł bratu swemu: Raka, będzie winien rady. A ktoby rzekł: Głupcze, będzie winien ognia piekielnego.
pl.5:23: Jeźli tedy ofiarujesz dar twój do ołtarza, a tam wspomnisz, iż brat twój ma nieco przeciw tobie,
pl.5:24: Zostaw tam dar twój przed ołtarzem a idź pierwéj zjednać się z bratem twoim: a tedy przyszedłszy ofiarujesz dar twój.
pl.5:25: Zgódź się z przeciwnikiem twoim rychło, pókiś jest z nim w drodze, by cię snadź przeciwnik nie podał sędziemu, a sędziaby cię podał słudze, a byłbyś wrzucon do ciemnice.
pl.5:26: Zaprawdę powiadam ci: Nie wynidziesz ztamtąd, aż oddasz ostatni pieniążek.
pl.5:27: Słyszeliście, iż powiedziano starym: Nie będziesz cudzołożył.
pl.5:28: A Ja powiadam wam, iż wszelki, który patrzy na niewiastę, aby jéj pożądał, już ją zcudzołożył w sercu swojem.
pl.5:29: Jeźli tedy prawe oko twoje gorszy cię, wyrwij je, a zarzuć od siebie; albowiem pożyteczniéj jest tobie, aby zginął jeden z członków twoich, niźliby miało być wrzucone wszystko ciało twoje do piekła.
pl.5:30: A jeźli cię prawa ręka twoja gorszy, odetnij ją i zarzuć od siebie; albowiem pożyteczniéj jest tobie, aby zginął jeden z członków twoich, niźliby miało iść wszystko ciało twoje do piekła.
pl.5:31: A powiedziano: Ktokolwiek opuści żonę swoję, niech jéj da list rozwodny.
pl.5:32: A Ja wam powiadam, iż wszelki, który opuści żonę swoje, wyjąwszy przyczynę porubstwa, czyni, że cudzołoży, i ktoby opuszczoną pojął, cudzołoży.
pl.5:33: Słyszeliście zasię, iż powiedziano starym: Nie będziesz krzywo przysięgał; ale oddasz Panu przysięgi twoje.
pl.5:34: A Ja wam powiadam, abyście zgoła nie przysięgali, ani na niebo; bo jest stolica Boża,
pl.5:35: Ani na ziemię; albowiem jest podnóżkiem nóg jego, ani na Jeruzalem; albowiem jest miasto wielkiego króla,
pl.5:36: Ani na głowę twoję będziesz przysięgał; albowiem nie możesz uczynić jednego włosa białym albo czarnym.
pl.5:37: A niechaj mowa wasza będzie: Jest, jest; Nie, nie. A co nad to więcéj jest, od złego jest.
pl.5:38: Słyszeliście, iż powiedziano: Oko za oko, a ząb za ząb.
pl.5:39: A Ja wam powiadam, żebyście się nie sprzeciwiali złemu: ale, jeźli cię kto uderzy w prawy policzek twój, nastaw mu i drugiego.
pl.5:40: A temu, który się chce z tobą prawem rozpierać a suknię twoję wziąć, puść mu i płaszcz.
pl.5:41: A ktoby cię kolwiek przymuszał na tysiąc kroków, idź z nim drugie dwa.
pl.5:42: A który cię prosi, daj mu, a od tego, który chce u ciebie pożyczyć, nie odwracaj się.
pl.5:43: Słyszeliście, iż powiedziano: Będziesz miłował bliźniego twego, a będziesz miał w nienawiści nieprzyjaciela twego.
pl.5:44: A Ja wam powiadam: Miłujcie nieprzyjacioły wasze, dobrze czyńcie tym, którzy was mają w nienawiści, a módlcie się za prześladujące i potwarzające was,
pl.5:45: Abyście byli synami Ojca waszego, który jest w niebiesiech, który czyni, że słońce jego wschodzi na dobre i złe, i spuszcza deszcz na sprawiedliwe i niesprawiedliwe.
pl.5:46: Albowiem jeźli miłujecie te, co was miłują, cóż za zapłatę mieć będziecie? azaż i celnicy tego nie czynią?
pl.5:47: A jeźlibyście pozdrawiali tylko bracią waszę, cóż więcej czynicie? azaż i poganie tego nie czynią?
pl.5:48: Bądźcież wy tedy doskonali, jako i Ojciec wasz niebieski doskonałym jest.
pl.6:1: Strzeżcie, abyście sprawiedliwości waszéj nie czynili przed ludźmi, abyście byli widziani od nich; bo inaczéj zapłaty mieć nie będziecie u Ojca waszego, który jest w niebiesiech.
pl.6:2: Gdy tedy czynisz jałmużnę, nie trąb przed sobą, jako obłudnicy czynią w bóżnicach i po ulicach, aby byli czczeni od ludzi; zaprawdę powiadam wam: Wzięli zapłatę swoję.
pl.6:3: Ale gdy ty czynisz jałmużnę, niechaj nie wie lewica twoja, co prawica twoja czyni,
pl.6:4: Aby jałmużna twoja była w skrytości: a Ojciec twój, który widzi w skrytości, odda tobie.
pl.6:5: A gdy się modlicie, nie będziecie jako obłudnicy, którzy się radzi w bóżnicach i na rogach ulic stojąc modlą, aby byli widziani od ludzi, zaprawdę powiadam wam: Wzięli zapłatę swoję.
pl.6:6: Ale ty gdy się modlić będziesz, wnidź do komory swojéj, a zawarłszy drzwi, módl się Ojcu twemu w skrytości: a Ojciec twój, który widzi w skrytości, odda tobie.
pl.6:7: A modląc się nie mówcie wiele, jako poganie; albowiem mniemają, iż w wielomowności swojéj będą wysłuchani.
pl.6:8: Nie bądźcież tedy im podobni; albowiemci wie Ojciec wasz, czego potrzebujecie, pierwéj niżbyście go prosili.
pl.6:9: Wy tedy tak się modlić będziecie: Ojcze nasz, któryś jest w niebiesiech! Święć się imię twoje.
pl.6:10: Przyjdź królestwo twoje. Bądź twa wola, jako w niebie tak i na ziemi.
pl.6:11: Chleba naszego powszedniego daj nam dzisiaj.
pl.6:12: I odpuść nam nasze winy, jako i my odpuszczamy naszym winowajcom.
pl.6:13: I nie wwódź nas w pokuszenie. Ale nas zbaw ode złego. Amen.
pl.6:14: Bo jeźli odpuścicie ludziom grzechy ich, odpuści téż wam Ojciec wasz niebieski grzechy wasze.
pl.6:15: Lecz jeźli nie odpuścicie ludziom, ani Ojciec wasz nie odpuści wam grzechów waszych.
pl.6:16: A gdy pościcie, nie bądźcie jako obłudnicy smętnymi; albowiem twarzy swoje niszczą, aby się ludziom zdali poszczącymi. Zaprawdę powiadam wam, iż wzięli zapłatę swoję.
pl.6:17: Ale ty kiedy pościsz, namaż głowę twoję i umyj oblicze swoje,
pl.6:18: Abyś się nie okazał ludziom, iż pościsz, ale Ojcu twemu, który jest w skrytości: a Ojciec twój, który widzi w skrytości, odda tobie.
pl.6:19: Nie skarbcie sobie skarbów na ziemi, gdzie rdza i mól psuje, i gdzie złodzieje wykopywają i kradną.
pl.6:20: Ale skarbcie sobie skarby w niebie, gdzie ani rdza, ani mól nie psuje, i gdzie złodzieje nie wykopują, ani kradną.
pl.6:21: Albowiem gdzie jest skarb twój, tam jest i serce twoje.
pl.6:22: Świecą ciała twego jest oko twoje. Jeźliby oko twoje było szczere, wszystko ciało twoje światłe będzie.
pl.6:23: Ale jeźliby oko twoje złe było, wszystko ciało twoje ciemne będzie. Jeźliż tedy światło, które jest w tobie, ciemnością jest, jakóż wielka będzie sama ciemność?
pl.6:24: Żaden nie może dwiema panom służyć; bo albo jednego będzie nienawidział a drugiego będzie miłował, albo przy jednym stać będzie, a drugim wzgardzi: nie możecie Bogu służyć i mammonie.
pl.6:25: Dlatego wam powiadam: Nie troszczcie się o duszę waszę, cobyście jedli, ani o ciało wasze, czembyście się odziewali. Azaż dusza nie jest ważniejsza niż pokarm? i ciało niźli odzienie?
pl.6:26: Wejrzyjcie na ptaki niebieskie, iż nie sieją ani żną, ani zbierają do gumien, a Ojciec wasz niebieski żywi je.
pl.6:27: Azażcie wy nie daleko ważniejsi niż oni? I kto z was obmyślając może przydać do wzrostu swego łokieć jeden?
pl.6:28: A o odzienie przecz się troszczycie? Przypatrzcie się liliom polnym, jako rosną: nie pracują, ani przędą.
pl.6:29: A powiadam wam, iż ani Salomon we wszystkiéj chwale swéj nie był odziany jako jedna z tych.
pl.6:30: A jeźliż trawę polną, która dziś jest, a jutro będzie w piec wrzucona, Bóg tak przyodziewa, jakoż daleko więcéj was małéj wiary?
pl.6:31: Nie troszczcież się tedy, mówiąc: Cóż będziem jeść, albo co będziem pić, albo czem się będziem przyodziewać.
pl.6:32: Bo tego wszystkiego poganie pilnie szukają; albowiem Ojciec wasz niebieski wie, że tego wszystkiego potrzebujecie.
pl.6:33: Szukajcież tedy najprzód królestwa Bożego i sprawiedliwości jego, a to wszystko będzie wam przydano.
pl.6:34: Nie troszczcież się tedy o jutrze; albowiem jutrzejszy dzień sam o się troskać się będzie. Dosyćci ma dzień na swéj nędzy.
pl.7:1: Nie sądźcie, abyście nie byli sądzeni.
pl.7:2: Albowiem którymbyście sądem sądzili, sądzeni będziecie, i którą miarą mierzyć będziecie, odmierzą wam.
pl.7:3: A cóż widzisz źdźbło w oku brata twego, a tramu w oku twojem nie widzisz?
pl.7:4: Albo jako mówisz bratu twemu: Dopuść, że wyjmę źdźbło z oka twego, a oto tram jest w oku twojem.
pl.7:5: Obłudniku! wyrzuć pierwéj tram z oka twego, a tedy przejrzysz, abyś wyrzucił źdźbło z oka brata twego.
pl.7:6: Nie dawajcie psom świętego, ani miećcie pereł waszych przed wieprze, by ich snadź nie podeptali nogami swemi, i obróciwszy się, aby was nie roztargali.
pl.7:7: Proście, a będzie wam dano; szukajcie, a najdziecie; kołaczcie, a będzie wam otworzono.
pl.7:8: Albowiem wszelki, który prosi, bierze; a kto szuka, najduje; a kołacącemu będzie otworzono.
pl.7:9: Albo któryż z was jest człowiek, którego jeźliby prosił syn jego o chleb, izali mu poda kamień?
pl.7:10: Albo jeźliby prosił o rybę, izali mu poda węża?
pl.7:11: Jeźli wy tedy, będąc złymi, umiecie datki dobre dawać synom waszym, jakóż więcéj Ojciec wasz, który jest w niebiesiech, da rzeczy dobre tym, którzy go proszą?
pl.7:12: Wszystko tedy, cokolwiek chcecie, aby wam ludzie czynili, i wy im czyńcie; boć ten jest zakon i prorocy.
pl.7:13: Wchódźcie przez ciasną bramę; albowiem szeroka brama i przestrona jest droga, która wiedzie na zatracenie, a wiele ich jest, którzy przez nię wchodzą.
pl.7:14: Jakóż ciasna brama i wązka jest droga, która wiedzie do żywota, a mało ich jest, którzy ją najdują.
pl.7:15: Strzeżcie się pilnie fałszywych proroków, którzy do was przychodzą w odzieniu owczem, a wewnątrz są wilcy drapieżni.
pl.7:16: Z owoców ich poznacie je. Izali zbierają z ciernia jagody winne, albo z ostu figi?
pl.7:17: Tak wszelkie drzewo dobre owoce dobre rodzi, a złe drzewo owoce złe rodzi.
pl.7:18: Nie może drzewo dobre owoców złych rodzić, ani drzewo złe owoców dobrych rodzić.
pl.7:19: Wszelkie drzewo, które nie rodzi owocu dobrego, będzie wycięte i w ogień wrzucone.
pl.7:20: A przeto z owoców ich poznacie je.
pl.7:21: Nie każdy, który mi mówi: Panie, Panie! wnidzie do królestwa niebieskiego; ale który czyni wolą Ojca mego, który jest w niebiesiech, ten wnidzie do królestwa niebieskiego.
pl.7:22: Wiele ich rzecze mi dnia onego: Panie, Panie! izaliśmy w imię twoje nie prorokowali i w imię twe czartów nie wyganiali i w imię twe wiele cudów nie czynili?
pl.7:23: A tedy wyznam im: Żem was nigdy nie znał, odstąpcie odemnie, którzy nieprawość czynicie.
pl.7:24: Wszelki tedy, który słucha tych słów moich i czyni je, będzie przypodobany mężowi mądremu, który zbudował dom swój na opoce.
pl.7:25: I spadł deszcz i przyszły rzeki i wiały wiatry i uderzyły na on dom, a nie upadł; bo był na opoce ugruntowany.
pl.7:26: A wszelki, który słucha tych słów moich, a nie czyni ich, będzie podobny mężowi głupiemu, który zbudował dom swój na piasku:
pl.7:27: I spadł deszcz i przyszły rzeki i wiały wiatry i uderzyły na on dom, i upadł, i był upadek jego wielki.
pl.7:28: I stało się, gdy dokończył Jezus tych słów, zdumiewały się rzesze nad nauką jego.
pl.7:29: Albowiem je uczył jako władzą mający, a nie jako Doktorowie ich i Pharyzeuszowie.
pl.8:1: A gdy zstąpił z góry, szły za nim wielkie rzesze.
pl.8:2: A oto trędowaty przyszedłszy, pokłonił się mu, mówiąc: Panie! jeźli chcesz, możesz mię oczyścić.
pl.8:3: I ściągnąwszy Jezus rękę, dotknął się go, mówiąc: Chcę, bądź oczyszczon. I był zarazem oczyszczon trąd jego.
pl.8:4: I rzekł mu Jezus: Patrz, abyś nikomu nie powiadał, ale idź, ukaż się kapłanowi i ofiaruj dar, który przykazał Mojżesz na świadectwo im,
pl.8:5: A gdy wszedł do Kapharnaum, przystąpił do niego setnik, prosząc go,
pl.8:6: I mówiąc: Panie! sługa mój leży w domu powietrzem ruszony i ciężko trapiony jest.
pl.8:7: I rzekł mu Jezus: Ja przyjdę, i uzdrowię go.
pl.8:8: I odpowiadając setnik, rzekł: Panie, nie jestem godzien, abyś wszedł pod dach mój; ale tylko rzecz słowem, a będzie uzdrowion sługa mój.
pl.8:9: Bo i ja jestem człowiek pod władzą postawiony, mający pod sobą żołnierze, i mówię temu: Idź, a idzie; a drugiemu: Chódź, a przychodzi, a słudze mojemu: Czyń to, a czyni.
pl.8:10: A usłyszawszy Jezus, dziwował się i rzekł tym, którzy szli z nim: Zaprawdę powiadam wam, nie nalazłem tak wielkiéj wiary w Izraelu.
pl.8:11: A powiadam wam, iż wiele ich ze wschodu słońca i z zachodu przyjdzie, i usiędą z Abrahamem i Izaakiem i Jakóbem w królestwie niebieskiem:
pl.8:12: A synowie królestwa będą wyrzuceni w ciemności zewnętrzne, tam będzie płacz i zgrzytanie zębów.
pl.8:13: I rzekł Jezus setnikowi: Idź, a jakoś uwierzył, niech ci się stanie. I uzdrowiony jest sługa onéj godziny.
pl.8:14: A gdy przyszedł Jezus do domu Piotrowego, ujrzał świekrę jego, leżącą a mającą gorączkę.
pl.8:15: I dotknął się ręki jéj, i opuściła ją gorączka, i wstała i posługowała im.
pl.8:16: A gdy był wieczór, przywiedli mu wiele djabelstwa mających, i wyrzucał duchy słowem, i wszystkie, którzy się źle mieli, uzdrowił:
pl.8:17: Aby się wypełniło, co jest rzeczono przez Izajasza proroka mówiącego: On niemocy nasze przyjął i choroby nasze nosił.
pl.8:18: A widząc Jezus wielkie rzesze około siebie, kazał jechać za morze.
pl.8:19: I przystąpiwszy jeden Doktor, rzekł mu: Nauczycielu! pójdę za tobą, gdzie jedno pójdziesz.
pl.8:20: I rzekł mu Jezus: Liszki mają jamy i ptacy niebiescy gniazda, a Syn człowieczy nie ma, gdzieby głowę skłonił.
pl.8:21: A drugi z uczniów jego rzekł mu: Panie! dopuść mi pierwéj odejść i pogrześć ojca mego.
pl.8:22: I rzekł mu Jezus: Pójdź za mną, a dopuść umarłym grześć umarłe swoje.
pl.8:23: A gdy on wstąpił w łódkę, weszli za nim uczniowie jego.
pl.8:24: A oto wzruszenie wielkie stało się na morzu, tak iż się łódka wałmi okrywała, a on spał.
pl.8:25: I przystąpili do niego uczniowie jego i obudzili go, mówiąc: Panie! zachowaj nas, giniemy.
pl.8:26: I rzekł im Jezus: Czemu bojaźliwi jesteście, małéj wiary? Tedy wstawszy rozkazał wiatrom i morzu, i stało się uciszenie wielkie.
pl.8:27: A ludzie się dziwowali, mówiąc: Jakiż jest ten, że mu i wiatry i morze są posłuszne?
pl.8:28: A gdy się przewieźli za morze do krainy Gerazeńczyków, zabieżeli mu dwaj mający djabelstwo, z grobów wychodzący, bardzo okrutni, tak iż żaden nie mógł przejść oną drogą.
pl.8:29: A oto zakrzyknęli, mówiąc: Co nam i tobie, Jezusie, synu Boży? przyszedłeś tu przed czasem męczyć nas?
pl.8:30: A było nie daleko od nich stado wiela wieprzów na paszéj.
pl.8:31: A czartowie prosili go, mówiąc: Jeźli nas wyrzucasz ztąd, puść nas w stado wieprzów.
pl.8:32: I rzekł im: Idźcie. A oni wyszedłszy, weszli w wieprze. A oto wszystko stado pędem z przykra wpadło w morze i pozdychało w wodach.
pl.8:33: A pasterze uciekli, i przyszedłszy do miasta, opowiedzieli wszystko i o onych, którzy mieli djabelstwo.
pl.8:34: A oto wszystko miasto wyszło przeciwko Jezusowi, i ujrzawszy go, prosili, aby z ich granic odszedł.
pl.9:1: I wstąpiwszy w łódkę, przewiózł się i przyszedł do miasta swego.
pl.9:2: A oto przynieśli mu powietrzem ruszonego, na łożu leżącego. A widząc Jezus wiarę ich, rzekł powietrzem ruszonemu: Ufaj, synu! odpuszczająć się grzechy twoje.
pl.9:3: A oto niektórzy z Doktorów mówili sami w sobie: Ten bluźni.
pl.9:4: A widząc Jezus myśli ich, rzekł: Przecz myślicie złe w sercach waszych?
pl.9:5: Cóż jest łacniéj rzec: Odpuszczająć się grzechy twoje? czyli rzec: Wstań a chódź?
pl.9:6: A iżbyście wiedzieli, że moc ma Syn człowieczy na ziemi odpuszczać grzechy, tedy rzekł powietrzem ruszonemu: Wstań, weźmij łoże twe, a idź do domu twego.
pl.9:7: I wstał i poszedł do domu swego.
pl.9:8: A ujrzawszy rzesze, bały się i chwaliły Boga, który dał takową moc ludziom.
pl.9:9: A gdy ztamtąd szedł Jezus, ujrzał człowieka siedzącego na cle, Mateusza imieniem. I rzekł mu: Pójdź za mną. A wstawszy poszedł za nim.
pl.9:10: I stało się, gdy on siedział u stołu w domu, oto wiele celników i grzeszników przyszedłszy, siedzieli u stołu z Jezusem i z uczniami jego.
pl.9:11: A widząc Pharyzeuszowie, mówili uczniom jego: Czemu z celniki i z grzeszniki je nauczyciel wasz?
pl.9:12: Lecz Jezus usłyszawszy, rzekł: Nie trzeba zdrowym lekarza, ale źle się mającym.
pl.9:13: A szedłszy nauczcie się, co jest: Miłosierdzia chcę, a nie ofiary; bom nie przyszedł wzywać sprawiedliwych, ale grzesznych.
pl.9:14: Tedy przystąpili do niego uczniowie Janowi, mówiąc: Przecz my i Pharyzeuszowie pościemy często, a uczniowie twoi nie poszczą?
pl.9:15: I rzekł im Jezus: Izali synowie oblubieńca smęcić się mogą, póki z nimi jest oblubieniec? Aleć przyjdą dni, gdy będzie wzięt od nich oblubieniec, a tedy będą pościć.
pl.9:16: A żaden nie wprawuje łaty surowego sukna w wiotchą szatę; albowiem obrywa od szaty całość jéj, i stawa się gorsze przedarcie.
